title: Understand Microsoft Fabric licenses (tenants, capacities, and SKUs)

claims.text: Each Fabric capacity is a distinct resource pool living inside a Microsoft Entra tenant; the SKU size determines how much compute power the pool provides, and a tenant can hold as many capacities as the organization needs — often aligned to geography or business unit.
Fabric F SKUs run from F2 up to F2048, and the SKU number equals its capacity units — an F64 supplies 64 CUs — with each step up the ladder doubling the compute of the previous size.

The Fabric trial grants a capacity equivalent to an F64 (64 CUs) for 60 days, behaving like F64 for Power BI viewing rights, which makes it a realistic sandbox for evaluating all Fabric experiences before purchase.

F64 is the licensing threshold for broad report consumption: on an F64 or larger capacity, users holding only a free Fabric license can view Power BI content if they have a workspace viewer role, whereas on smaller F SKUs every viewer needs a Pro or PPU license.

Microsoft is consolidating purchase options around Fabric F SKUs and retiring the Power BI Premium per-capacity P SKUs; the documentation maps F64 to the former P1 (8 v-cores) for compute comparison only, not licensing equivalence.

Relying on Power BI Premium Per User (PPU) licenses to run Fabric workloads is a mistake: PPU is a per-user feature set, not a capacity, so it cannot create or run non-Power BI Fabric items such as lakehouses, warehouses, or notebooks — an F or Trial capacity is still required.

Every Fabric-enabled tenant includes a shared capacity that hosts all personal My Workspaces plus Pro and PPU workspace types; new workspaces land on this shared capacity by default and can later be reassigned to any capacity in the tenant.

A workspace's type (formerly called license mode) dictates which kind of capacity backs it — Fabric F SKU, Power BI Premium P SKU, or the shared Pro/PPU pools — and therefore which experiences its users can run; only Fabric, Trial, and P-SKU workspace types support all Fabric experiences.

Workspaces on Fabric F SKUs gain Azure-integration capabilities not available elsewhere, including ARM APIs, Terraform support, and managed private endpoints — relevant when architecting for infrastructure-as-code or private networking.

A free Fabric per-user license is granted automatically the first time someone signs in to the Fabric portal (when the tenant has Fabric enabled), and it permits creating and sharing non-Power BI Fabric items in workspaces backed by an F or Trial capacity.

Creating Power BI items outside a personal My Workspace and sharing them always requires a Pro or PPU per-user license regardless of capacity size, so any organization using Power BI within Fabric needs at least one Pro or PPU licensed user.
Power BI Embedded A SKUs and EM SKUs support only Power BI items, not Fabric items, so embedding architectures that also need lakehouses or other Fabric workloads must pair them with an F capacity.
